Definition: from G308; restoration of sight:--recovery of sight.
BiblicalUsage: The word appears once, in the words Jesus read in the synagogue at Nazareth from Isaiah: the Spirit of the Lord is upon me, to preach the gospel to the poor, to heal the brokenhearted, to preach deliverance to the captives, and recovering of sight to the blind. It is the noun for getting sight back — the thing the blind receive when the Messiah comes.
TheologicalSignificance: One word for recovery of sight carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the promise Jesus read aloud and claimed — the blind see, because He has come.
